newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-LEANEY KEEPS LEAD AS BAKER-FINCH MISSES CUT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEANEY KEEPS LEAD AS BAKER-FINCH MISSES CUT.

text.p: Former British Open champion Ian Baker-Finch failed to make the halfway cut in his comeback tournament on Friday after carding a second round of two-over-par 74 in the Victorian Open.

Baker-Finch, who has made the halfway cut in only one tournament in more than two years, finished a massive 15 shots behind leader and fellow Australian Stephen Leaney, who shot an even-par 72 to maintain a two-stroke lead on eight-under 136.
Euan Walters of Australia was second on 138 after a round of 69. Terry Price, Rodney Pampling and Paul Barnsley, all of Australia, were tied for third another stroke back on 139.
Baker-Finch, winner of the 1991 British Open, was returning to tournament golf after a self-imposed absence of six months.
The affable Australian finished on 151 to miss the cut by four shots but was not disappointed with his performance.
"I saw some improvement and my short game was really good," said Baker-Finch, who had not played in a tournament since missing the cut at the British Open last July.
"At this stage it's just a rebuilding process. I really would have liked to have played the next two days here for the practice," he said.
Leaney set a course record of 64 in Thursday's first round but later said he was content with a 72 after swirling wind and quickening greens made conditions more difficult.
"I didn't expect to hit four or five-under and anything from par to 70 I would have been happy with," Leaney said.
